title: MYP to DP: What Changes and How to Prepare
summary: MYP to DP explained clearly: understand changes in subjects, assessment, workload and independence, with practical preparation advice for families.
body_markdown:
Imagine an MYP student opening their new DP timetable. The subjects look familiar. Mathematics is still mathematics. Biology still involves cells, systems and evidence. English still asks for close reading. Yet the timetable feels different because each choice now carries more weight.


That is the central change from **MYP to DP** . Students move from the broad, connected framework of the IB Middle Years Programme into a two-year course built around six selected subjects, studied at standard level or higher level, alongside the DP core. The content becomes deeper, assessment becomes more consequential, and independent planning matters more.


This transition can feel abrupt, but it is not a leap into an entirely unfamiliar system. MYP has already developed many of the habits DP rewards: inquiry, reflection, communication, research and applying knowledge in context. The task is to make those habits more deliberate.


### MYP to DP at a glance


Area What changes in DP


Subject structure Eight broad MYP subject groups give way to six selected DP subjects plus the core


Depth Students study fewer areas but explore chosen subjects in greater depth


Course levels At least three and no more than four subjects are taken at higher level, with the rest at standard level


Assessment Subject-specific internal work and external assessment carry greater weight


Independence Students must manage overlapping deadlines, revision and long-term projects


Core requirements Theory of knowledge, the extended essay and creativity, activity, service become part of the programme


Before choosing courses, students and parents should review the school's available combinations, entry guidance and timetable restrictions. RevisionDojo's[guide to preparing for the transition from MYP to DP](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/prepare-for-transition-from-myp-to-dp) provides a useful starting framework.


### The curriculum becomes narrower and deeper


The[IB Middle Years Programme subjects](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-subjects-are-taught-in-myp) span eight groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, design, and physical and health education. This breadth encourages students to see connections across disciplines.


In the DP, students normally study six subjects. They take at least three and no more than four at higher level, with the remainder at standard level. Higher level courses cover a greater body of knowledge and require more teaching time, but both levels demand serious engagement.


For our hypothetical MYP student, this creates the first difficult question: not simply, “Which subject do I enjoy?” but, “Which subjects am I prepared to study consistently for two years?”


Interest matters because it sustains attention. Current performance matters because it reveals foundations. Future university requirements may matter too. None of these should be considered alone.


Students can compare their present preparation through RevisionDojo's[MYP subject and assessment overview](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp-syllabus) . Those considering different mathematical pathways can review the[MYP Standard Mathematics resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics) and[MYP Extended Mathematics resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-extended-mathematics) . Science students can similarly identify strengths and gaps using the[MYP Integrated Sciences subject page](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-integrated-sciences) .


### Assessment feels more cumulative


MYP assessment is criterion-related. Teachers assess work against published subject criteria, and the programme emphasizes demonstrating skills in varied contexts. In the final MYP year, students complete the personal project independently. Other MYP eAssessment components are optional for schools, so the exact experience can differ between campuses.


DP assessment remains broader than a single examination session. It combines externally assessed components with internally completed work that is assessed or moderated according to IB procedures. The balance and format vary by subject. Many courses also culminate in substantial externally marked examination components.


The practical difference is accumulation. A weak week in MYP can often be followed by a fresh task and a clean start. In DP, unfinished notes, uncertain concepts and delayed coursework can quietly gather interest, like a small debt that becomes expensive because it was ignored.


This is why students should learn to respond to feedback immediately. RevisionDojo's Questionbank and AI grading tools can help turn comments into targeted practice. Study Notes clarify the underlying idea, while Flashcards support repeated recall. The aim is not to collect more resources. It is to shorten the distance between discovering a weakness and fixing it.


A student with a backpack learns that a calendar may be more useful for DP


### The DP core adds three continuing commitments


The six subjects are only part of the programme. Diploma students also complete three core elements.


### Theory of knowledge


Theory of knowledge, usually called TOK, asks students to examine how knowledge is produced, justified and communicated. It is assessed through an exhibition and a 1,600-word essay under current IB guidance. MYP students have already practised reflection and inquiry, but TOK makes those habits more explicit.


### The extended essay


The extended essay is an independent research project culminating in a paper of up to 4,000 words. The important transition is not merely writing more. Students must define a manageable research question, select appropriate evidence, develop an argument and reflect on their process.


The MYP personal project offers useful preparation. It teaches students to sustain work over time rather than relying on last-minute energy. RevisionDojo's Coursework Library, grading tools and Tutors can support the development of research and writing skills, while the student's own work must always follow school and IB academic integrity requirements.


### Creativity, activity, service


Creativity, activity, service, known as CAS, requires students to pursue experiences beyond conventional academic study. CAS is not spare time that happens after the “real” work. It is part of the programme and therefore needs space in the calendar from the beginning.


### Time management becomes visible


In MYP, a capable student can sometimes depend on memory, quick understanding and a burst of effort before a deadline. DP exposes the limits of that strategy.


Consider the hypothetical student again. On Monday, there is no crisis. There is only a science report due in two weeks, an English passage to annotate, a mathematics topic that feels slightly uncertain and an extended essay meeting next month. The danger is not difficulty alone. It is the absence of urgency.


A workable weekly system should include:


- fixed review periods for each higher level subject;
- shorter retrieval sessions for standard level courses;
- one block for internal work or the extended essay;
- time for CAS and rest;
- a weekly check of deadlines and unresolved feedback.


RevisionDojo's AI Chat can help students question unfamiliar ideas, but it should support thinking rather than replace it. Predicted Papers and Mock Exams become most useful after the relevant content has been learned, when timed practice can reveal gaps in knowledge, interpretation and pacing.


### Parents move from monitoring to supporting


Parents often notice the transition before students describe it. The calendar becomes fuller, results may fluctuate, and a student who previously seemed effortlessly organized may suddenly appear overwhelmed.


The most useful response is not constant surveillance. It is calm structure. Ask what deadlines are approaching, which subject currently requires the most attention and what support the school offers. A weekly conversation is generally more constructive than daily questions about grades.


Parents should also remember that subject selection is local as well as academic. Schools differ in the courses they offer, how subjects fit into timetable blocks and what preparation they recommend. The[comparison of MYP and the Diploma Programme](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-myp-vs-ib-diploma-programme-key-differences-and-progression) can help families understand the broad progression, but the school's DP coordinator remains essential for decisions about an individual timetable.


### What students should do before DP begins


Preparation does not mean trying to teach yourself the entire DP curriculum during a holiday. That often creates exhaustion without secure understanding.


Instead, review foundations in the subjects you intend to continue. Identify recurring weaknesses. Practise writing explanations, not just remembering answers. Build a calendar system and learn to divide a large task into smaller deadlines. Students wondering when this process should begin can use RevisionDojo's guidance on[when to start preparing for DP during MYP](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/when-should-i-start-preparing-for-dp-while-still-in-myp) .


RevisionDojo brings that preparation together through MYP and DP Study Notes, Questionbank practice, Flashcards, AI Chat, grading support, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, the Coursework Library and Tutors. Its[complete collection of MYP resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp) allows students to strengthen the foundations they have now before choosing the depth they will pursue next.


### A transition, not a reinvention


Moving from MYP to DP changes the scale of the work, not the identity of the learner. Curiosity still matters. Reflection still matters. Clear communication and honest self-assessment matter even more.


The student looking at that new timetable does not need to become perfectly organized overnight. They need a reliable way to notice what matters, begin before urgency arrives and seek help before uncertainty becomes a backlog. With its connected learning, practice, assessment and tutoring tools, RevisionDojo is the ultimate IB resource for making that transition with purpose rather than panic.
